reason: B opens inside the smoke at Naseby and then moves to the walls of Constantinople, so the administrative argument about arsenals, tax farms and Tokugawa control arrives attached to scenes a general reader is already invested in. A front-loads eight sections of inventory-and-treasury exposition before its one vivid passage (Magdeburg) at the very end, and it repeatedly restates the same thesis - the gun depends on clerks, powder and payment - in near-identical phrasing across the Ottoman, French, Dutch, Mughal and English sections. B still returns to its thesis but each return sits on new material, giving a stronger sense of forward movement rather than circling.
